page: Amazon Web Services g7e.12xlarge is an x86_64 server instance optimized for graphics and compute-heavy workloads running on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 2.4 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 (BF16 and VNNI). Memory capacity stands at 512 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, providing approximately 10.67 GB per physical core. For compute acceleration, the server includes two NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs delivering a combined 192 GB of VRAM. High-speed local storage is provided via a 3800 GB NVMe SSD array, supported by a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark results demonstrate high processing capability across AI and compute-intensive tasks. In LLM inference tests, the instance reaches top-tier performance, producing prompt processing throughput of up to 11238.84 tokens per second on small 135M models and 1264.93 tokens per second on 70B models, alongside text generation speeds of 28.25 tokens per second on 70B models. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth register strong outputs at 225.52 GB/s and 96.28 GB/s respectively. Additional benchmarks show high efficiency in data manipulation, including a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 340.41 GB/s, static web serving throughput of 86.87 GB/s, and a Redis SET capability of 69.67 million operations per second.

The hardware combination of 512 GB DDR5 RAM, dual GPUs, and high-speed NVMe storage provides strong resource density for large-scale graphics and machine learning workloads without local storage bottlenecks. However, stress-ng CPU tests indicate middle-tier multi-core processor performance relative to dedicated high-core compute instances, meaning CPU-bound tasks without GPU or matrix instruction utilization may not maximize hardware investments. Given its massive VRAM, high network bandwidth, and Intel AMX matrix extensions, the g7e.12xlarge is optimal for LLM inference, generative AI modeling, real-time ray tracing, large dataset processing, and high-throughput web service deployment.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.12xlarge is a graphics-intensive x86_64 instance built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. Powered by a 24-core Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz, it offers 48 vCPUs with AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. The system integrates 512 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, dual NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing 192 GB of total VRAM, a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, and 400 Gbps network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight top-tier LLM inference speeds across 7B and 70B parameter models, combined with strong memory bandwidth reaching 225.52 GB/s for uncached reads. While multi-core CPU benchmarks reflect average raw compute performance, the server excels in accelerated workloads. The g7e.12xlarge provides high resource density, making it well-suited for large language model serving, advanced AI inference, image and ray-tracing rendering, high-concurrency Redis instances, and memory-intensive data analytics.
